For the physicist: f4b.py's per-pair least squares (3 x 3 Gram, 3 x 2 design, batched 2 x 2 solve) has a closed form that needs only the Gram of the pair's two gated columns. Write the hub's quartic on the pair's own columns P = Y + t+ Wt, Q = Y + t- Wt: five coefficients fixed at birth, Psi_m = (t+ - t-)^-4 sum_{i<=4-m, j<=m} binom(4-m,i) binom(m,j) (-1)^j (-t-)^(4-m-i) t+^(m-j) S_(i+j). Then x+ = (d/2)[(Psi0 + k+ Psi1) P^2 + 2 (Psi1 + k+ Psi2) P Q + (Psi2 + k+ Psi3) Q^2], x- = (d/2)[(Psi2 + k- Psi1) P^2 + 2 (Psi3 + k- Psi2) P Q + (Psi4 + k- Psi3) Q^2], with k+ = 2 spq sqq / (spp sqq + spq^2), k- = 2 spq spp / (spp sqq + spq^2) and spp, spq, sqq the inner products of the two gated columns. Rule A (F4) is exactly Psi = (A lam+, 0, 0, 0, A lam-); K4L's local term is sum_m binom(4,m) Psi_m P^(4-m) Q^m. Checked against f4b.py's arithmetic in float64: 1e-15 (O/engineer/a18_f4b/check_projection.py). The reason is the spectrum: at layer 12 the eigenvalues 1 / 2 / 8 / 16 / 17 / 32 are 0.062 / 0.032 / 0.020 / 0.014 / 0.014 / 0.0084 of the trace, so the 16th and 17th are not separated; at layers 1-2 the spectrum is flat (first over 32nd = 1.3-1.5) and no scheme finds 'the' top eigenvectors there. A join projects the joined columns on its rank-r frame; the third-order norm-coupling vector of those columns, t_c = sum_r lam_r |J_r|^2 J_rc (the same quantity as the star's row sums, section 17 of my RESULT.md), changes by 1.25% at the layer-7 join (rank 384), 2.30% at layer 10 (rank 320) and 1.02% at layer 13 (rank 384), although the joins lose only 0.03%, 0.03% and 0.002% of the columns' energy (O/engineer/a35_join/probe_join.py, network 651, the estimator's own columns, the join repeated in float64). Lever JR (O/engineer/a35_join/fragment_jr_v1.py): the miss is computed at the join (two passes over the joined columns) and its coherent part m_i (W' miss)_j is added to the transported star of the join layer, three times that on the diagonal; +0.044% bill, +84 calls. (1) THE SECOND WEIGHT is one more vector of the bank's length next to lam: same roster, extended with zeros where lam is extended at the births. The joins, the alive mask and the push need NOTHING: they act on the columns, the weights only ride along. The old tier needs no second core natively: its columns are rebuilt on the read's rows in every layer anyway, so its weights are just the leading entries of the same vector. (2) THE RECURSION at the end of a layer, w <- 2 (gbar w + lam o (V' pp)): one matrix-vector product over the layer's pushed columns (2 n R flops); V = 2 m (1 - g) and gbar = mean(g - m pdf / sigma) are per-unit vectors the loop holds (m after the learned correction, as your out[0]). (3) THE READ. Natively the plane is left2 (right o lam)' for the young columns and ((left2 o lam) F') U' for the old tier, with left2 = pp^2 on the response rows. Both are linear in left2 and multiply by lam afterwards, so the fold is ONE elementwise change of left2 before the read: left2_ir <- left2_ir - f_i pp_ir (w_r / lam_r), f_i = strength mu_i / (n v_i). The old tier's inner product in u/v form takes any left factor, so it needs no change; no kernel shape changes; nothing in setup. Cost: one gather of pp on the response rows and three elementwise passes over rows x columns. (4) THE FORMS. The least squares on the off-diagonal of B is NOT available natively (sum_ij B_ij C_ij needs C pp, a full product over the columns). Available: the diagonal B_ii = (pp^2) w on the response rows (one matrix-vector product, the rows where every column is rebuilt), a regression with 3-4 unknowns on per-unit vectors, and the form planes added on the read's block (elementwise on rows x live columns; C mu is one n^2 product). A per-layer CONSTANT times tr C x C would need neither B_ii nor a regression: physicist, if your arm with a constant holds, that is the form to port. (5) BILL, at the S39 bill of 2.513e11 flops: the bank has about 1,600 columns per cohort, so 3,000 to 22,000 columns from layer 2 to 14 (mean 12,800), and about 800 response rows: fold of the left factor 41 Mflop a layer, recursion 26, B_ii 20, forms 8: about 95 Mflop a layer, 1.2 Gflop a network = 0.5% OF THE BILL (0.4% with a constant instead of the regression), not 0.15%: the passes over rows x all columns are the price. Requests about 15-20 a layer, 250 a network (S39 has about 700 of room). [trainer] 2026-10-02 17:53 UTC — CAN THE HEAD'S INPUT LAYER TAKE A NEW COLUMN WITHOUT RETRAINING? YES (lead 17:52Z). The learned mean correction is: 30 standardised per-unit features + 96 message columns = 126 inputs -> enc0 (128 x 126, silu) -> enc2 (128 x 128, silu) -> enc4 (64) = the unit's state -> per-layer head (64 weights + bias); the state also feeds the next layer's messages. A 127th input column with ZERO weights in enc0 leaves every prediction bit for bit as it is; what is new is 128 numbers (its column of enc0_w, the same for all layers) plus one centre and one scale per layer, and those 128 weights can be solved alone like dials. In torch I add it as a per-unit term in enc0's bias (bias + z_i u', u a zero leaf of 128), so the gradient of u at zero is exact and nothing else is touched; natively it is one more value in the feature function and one more column in the enc0 literal. THE TEST AS ASKED (gradient of the new weights at zero over the training networks, |t| above 3 -> a small solve of the 128 weights) is being built now for the six per-unit numbers of the lead's list (diagonal residual of the law's matrix over tr C v_i; row norm and signed row sum against the correlation of the law's fold term; the same two for the k31l term; fitted diagonal over B_ii); it rides on the gradient runs of the learned-array test, so it costs no extra pass for 18 of the 36 networks. With 128 weights per feature about 0.35 of them pass |t| > 3 by chance, so I will report per feature the count beyond 3 and the mean of t squared over the 128 (1.0 under no signal, sd 0.125).

What the two columns are (engineer/a22_cutsim/torch_rowcuts_v15.py lines 88-134): at layers 7-14 the native card zeroes the pushed old-tier columns of up to 64 'tail' rows (alpha > 2.5, or alpha < -2.5 and dead) and the young columns of the dead tail (alpha < -2.5), and puts back a cheap estimate of those rows' k3 diagonal ('repair'); HU31/32 = that estimate / (v s), nonzero ONLY on the cut rows. So the columns can at most teach the head the error of the repair on those rows. Ceiling measured directly: S46 with the v11 cut simulator (the certified native-faithful torch card, pinned profile, sources unchanged since the bridge) on the lead's fit seeds 7100136-151, three arms per seed: A = native cuts as fired, B = the tails exact (no cut, no repair), C = cut with the repair removed. B - A bounds what any learned use of the repair can recover; C - A says how much the repair amplitude matters at all. One worker, 3 threads, nice 10 (physicist/t90_repair_ceiling/, 48 runs, about 60-75 min). The LS head-row fit follows only if B - A leaves room for -0.4%.

- v50j (full-trace core) smoke, ranks 35/200: raw +3.5% / +6.7%, ADJUSTED +3.75% / +6.60% (L11-12 better, L13-14 worse again). The core was not the cause.
- Cause (joinsketch/join_basis_v13/v14.py + jsk/probe_kernel_noise_v1.py): the estimator's Winograd kernels (_CP3_WINOGRAD_LEVELS 4) round 10-25x worse than BLAS (Frobenius rel 4-8e-6, max-normalised 2e-6..1e-5 on the real sketch operands). Emulating that noise offline collapses every whitened power-step variant (eps 3e-7: plane error 2.5-4x TODAY's; mu-regularised or shifted variants either collapse or lose the whole gain) while today's single-product Nystrom sketch is unmoved (eps 1e-6: +0.5%). Mechanism: the step's gain lives in the tail directions it lifts; after the step those sit at the kernel's noise floor and are replaced by garbage.
- Noise-robust alternatives at today's cost all lose: sparse +-1 test vectors over 2-4 rows (+8-10% plane error vs coordinate rows), shifted steps (= Nystrom at best). A BLAS-accurate (plain matmul) JSK costs 1.7x the billed flops of the fast sketch: the configuration at today's bill (kc 1024, plain) keeps only the L10/L13 gains (~-8% basis) for +0.6% bill once the old-tier terms are made plain too -> adjusted ~+0.2%. CLOSED.
- Side finding: rotating TODAY's frame to its principal coordinates cuts the u-leg (leading-256-coordinate) truncation error 13-17% at every join, but needs an eigh (9n^3 = 0.51 GF/join, +0.8% bill with the rotation) for an estimated -0.2..-0.3% MSE: not a lever. Coordinate-order heuristics (pair-mean energy) do nothing.
- Lesson for any future sketch work: price in kernel noise (4e-6) and requests (~70 per kernel product); the Nystrom single product is noise-optimal.
